claim.claim: Alphabet's results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 show that generative AI is not cannibalizing its search advertising business.

verdict.label: SUPPORTED

supporting_evidence.quote: Google Search & other revenues increased $6.8 billion and $25.6 billion from the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025 to the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.

The overall growth was driven by interrelated factors including increases in search queries resulting from growth in user adoption and usage on mobile devices; growth in advertiser spending; and improvements we have made in ad formats and delivery.

verdict.reasoning_summary:
The claim asserts that generative AI is not cannibalizing Alphabet's search advertising business for Q3 2026. This is an interpretive claim about the absence of a negative effect.

The evidence shows that Google Search & other revenues (which represents search advertising) increased substantially in Q3 2026:
- Q3 2026: $63,350 million vs Q3 2025: $56,567 million (an increase of $6.8 billion)
- The filing attributes this growth to "increases in search queries resulting from growth in user adoption and usage on mobile devices; growth in advertiser spending; and improvements we have made in ad formats and delivery"

The strong growth in search advertising revenues during this period supports the claim that generative AI is not cannibalizing the search advertising business. If cannibalization were occurring, we would expect to see declining or stagnant revenues, not the substantial growth observed. The evidence affirmatively establishes that the search advertising business grew significantly during Q3 2026, which is consistent with the absence of cannibalization.

This is a purely interpretive claim about the absence of a negative causal relationship, not a numeric claim about specific figures or thresholds.

H2 (Growth from pricing masking volume declines): CHALLENGE_REFUTED - Evidence E14 shows that for the six months ended June 30, 2026, paid clicks increased 13% while cost-per-click increased only 3-4%. This demonstrates that growth was driven primarily by volume (clicks) rather than pricing, refuting the hypothesis that pricing increases masked underlying volume declines. Similarly, E13 shows 2025 had 6% paid clicks growth and 7% cost-per-click growth - both positive.

H3 (AI features reducing monetization): NO_RELEVANT_EVIDENCE - While E15 mentions AI Overviews and notes that AI integration "may monetize differently" and "could affect revenue growth rates," this is a forward-looking statement about potential future effects, not evidence of actual cannibalization occurring in Q3 2026. The statement is cautionary and does not indicate that AI features are currently reducing ad clicks or monetization.

The evidence continues to support that search advertising grew substantially in Q3 2026, with both volume (paid clicks) and revenue increasing, which is inconsistent with cannibalization occurring during this period.

We expect that this evolution, including user engagement with AI products and services, will continue to benefit our business and our revenues. As we continue to incorporate AI into our products and services, such as with AI Overviews and AI Mode in Search, and with enterprise AI solutions on our Google Cloud Platform, we may monetize differently than our historical consumer and enterprise offerings which could affect revenue growth rates and margin trends. When developing new products and services we generally focus first on user experience and then on monetization. At the same time, we face increasing competition, including from other developers and providers of AI products and services, which may affect our revenues. Increasing Revenues Beyond Advertising: Revenues from cloud, consumer subscriptions, platforms, and devices, which may have differing characteristics than our advertising revenues, have grown over time. Certain of these revenues have been growing at a rate higher than our advertising revenues, becoming a larger percentage of our consolidated revenues, and we expect this trend to continue.
